title: Using machine-learning to screen for PTSD after childhood trauma
summary:
Around every second child experiences at least one potentially traumatizing event (PTE). Such events can have long-term negative psychological consequences. Nevertheless, many of those affected are neither diagnosed in time nor treated adequately. Research findings show that acute stress symptoms that occur within the first four weeks after the PTE are a reliable predictor for the development of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Early recognition of these symptoms therefore plays a crucial role in prevention.
The aim of this study is machine learning-based symptom screening and prediction of PTSD symptoms in adolescents with childhood trauma. To date, researchers have successfully used digital biomarkers - such as facial expressions, speech, non-verbal characteristics and eye and head movements - to classify and monitor PTSD in adults. In children and adolescents, such approaches have so far only been used for other disorders. For this study, adolescents aged 12 to 18 years admitted to the Department of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, Psychosomatics and Psychotherapy who have been exposed to various PTEs, as well as adolescents admitted to the Department of Trauma, Hand and Reconstructive Surgery following a traumatic injury, will be included in the study. PTSD symptoms will be assessed using a standardized clinical interview. In addition, short free interviews will be conducted as part of the trauma exploration in order to identify digital biomarkers later. In addition, several questionnaires will be completed by the adolescents and caregivers. The survey takes place at two measurement points four weeks apart.

interventions.name: Adolescents who have experienced psychological potentially traumatizing experiences (PTE) and are being treated for psychiatric/psychological symptoms and adolescents who have experienced physical PTE and are being treated for surgical symptoms. Systematic surveys are carried out on all participants

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
(1)	Treatment at the Clinic for Trauma, Hand, Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery or the Clinic for Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, Psychosomatics and Psychotherapy
(2)	A DSM-5-compliant PTE or a potentially traumatic injury requiring treatment
(3)	No severe traumatic brain injury (Glasgow Coma Score < 13)
(4)	Sufficient knowledge of the German language
(5)	Signed declaration of consent from adolescents and their parents/guardians; adolescents aged 16 and over may also participate without the consent of their parents/guardians
(6)	In possession of an e-mail address (due to sending links and agreement of measurement time 2 examination)
(7)	In possession of a smartphone/tablet/laptop/PC (online survey)
Exclusion criteria:
result exclusively from inclusion criteria (e.g. Glasgow Coma Scale <13)
